title: Face study · A head seated in the collar
summary: The owner selected the stamped head, split collar and red upper arms from v003 as the starting point for [Mantle](#/occult-ritual-mechs/7). That frame develops the collar into shoulder-to-shoulder armor over a slimmer biomechanical body.

items.title: Marked mask and recessed teeth · v003
items.alt: A close-up and full-body view of the same four-weapon mech. Its stamped pewter face has a line of dark slots and small teeth beneath the chin. Slotted round fasteners sit in the cheek, chest and red upper arm.
items.body:
The mask openings suggest one mouth at a distance. Up close, a second line of blunt ivory teeth sits in shadow below the chin. Stamped characters wrap over the crown and temple. The white R04 stencil follows the grain of the shoulder fibers, while the same slotted fastener appears in the cheek, chest and outer arm. The teeth are more regular and grin-like than those in the reference. This treatment is exploratory.

The full-body view shows a long accelerator and a short pulse emitter in the hands. A missile cassette and twin-barrel unit rise from separate rear pivots. The compact side jets remain visible at the hips.

**References used.** All three images were supplied directly to the built-in image generator. The [v002 sheet](assets/face-study/front-rear-v002.png) supplied the chassis and loadout. The [owner’s circled reference](references/face-study/smooth-mask-owner-markup.png) selected the mask openings, the row beneath the chin, the surface lettering and the arm fastener. The [clean portrait](references/pinterest/smooth-mask-788411478568823397.jpg) supplied the details underneath the markup. [Original pin](https://www.pinterest.com/pin/788411478568823397/)

[Open full-resolution PNG](assets/face-study/marked-mask-v003.png)
items.prompt:
Make one new reference-guided variant of IMAGE 1 (our fleet Face study v002). IMAGE 2 is the owner's markup of the portrait in IMAGE 3. The red hand-drawn circles select the small horizontal holes ON the mask, the separate shadowed row of teeth UNDER the mask, and the stamped striated upper arm with its flush circular attachment. Use image 3 to see those features uninterrupted. Never render the red annotation. Rework the head and upper arms noticeably in that direction while preserving a convincing armed, walking and boosting machine from the fleet in image 1. One well composed, wide landscape concept plate in exactly two views of the SAME design and markings: left half a large intimate near-frontal portrait of head, collar and near upper arm; right half a complete front three-quarter view of the whole armed vehicle, every gun and both feet inside the canvas. Neutral warm gray backdrop and light space for silhouettes, quiet side light that reaches under the chin.

Primary design experiment: smooth, abraded smoke-pewter face with tranquil almost-erased brow and blank temples; SMALL head nested in the divided hull collar. Across the LOWER mask put a short uneven horizontal line of five dark punched slots. Below that, under the metal chin and inside the black throat seal, create a second mouth-like structure: a partly open seam with a clearly visible close row of little blunt ivory ceramic contact teeth seated deep in dark graphite gums. They are slightly uneven at the tips; the upper lip of metal casts a shadow over them. It should be possible to notice the slots first and then catch sight of the teeth lower down. Give them real definition in the large close-up. At vehicle scale it reads as an unsettling pale glimmer, not a grinning skull. No lips, human nose, bright side eye, giant fangs or open snarl. Dark side optic like a recessed fitting. Existing variant's split collar opens just enough to show this detail.

Surface and markings are a principal feature. Make the worn machine feel repeatedly numbered, stamped and serviced. Wrap narrow arcs of small oxblood inspection stamps and charcoal batch codes obliquely over the pewter temple and crown; a broken vertical string of tiny numerals near one temple. Retain clean breathing room around the face. Choose a few specific stencils for crisp legibility, "C-17" on the temple and "R04" in chalk-white on the near burgundy arm tissue; also echo small faded maintenance marks on the collar, chest, hips and gun housings. Some painted strokes catch in the striations across that arm. These marks exist on the parts, not as captions; no external typography, plate titles or drawings printed OVER the picture. Integrate the circled screw-like motif as shallow circular steel rings around a dark recessed slot: one near lower cheek, one seated flush into a rigid insert in the marked arm and a few others of different diameters on the sternum and hips. They should look captive and almost grown into the casing; avoid a uniform polka-dot pattern.

Arms: withdraw the outer shoulder plate modestly and expose a crescent of tightly striated dark red tissue which rolls into the upper arm around its large steel bearing. The large head detail includes at least one shoulder and its arm stamp plus ring. Keep the field-machine proportions, strong graphite legs, visible rear booster skirt in side profile and separate recessed hip jets. On the full body view show exactly FOUR weapons seen at once: a long square open-channel accelerator gripped low in anatomical right hand (viewer left), a much shorter broad ceramic emitter gripped in anatomical left (viewer right); above and behind them a square cell cassette on the right back pivot and a long folded twin-rail gun on the left back pivot. Hands visibly around underslung grips. Both back units have exposed pinned swing arms rooted in the hull with air between each weapon and the shoulder. Slightly stagger their heights, leave gaps between all 4 weapon silhouettes. Compact pilot hull and weight-bearing, springy legs from image 1. Four complete distinguishable weapons on the full-body view; the close-up is a detail of that very machine. Distinct markings consistent between views. Use the anatomical reference as selective inspiration for the face language, surface stamps and circular attachments; no copied silhouette or spikes. A restrained polished piece of visual development with worn industrial paint, rich graphite and dark wine tissue, dim cold pewter, a little warm bone color. No lore graphics, horns or ornate symbols.

items.title: Slim frame direction · Continued as Mantle
items.body:
The owner prefers the v003 head, split collar and red upper arms. The [Mantle tab](#/occult-ritual-mechs/7) carries this direction forward. Use those shapes as the starting point. The current game plan gives each chassis its own body parts, so the rest of the silhouette can be tailored to this frame.

**Shape and loadout.** Keep the head low and the red upper arms visible beneath the collar. Simple forearm guards leave room for a full-size hand weapon. Cut back the broad outer shoulders, pull in the flanks, and give the cockpit its volume front to back. Seen head-on there is daylight between each elbow and the waist. In profile the cockpit has depth, and the hips, thighs and heels can still catch the equipped frame on landing. Extend the fixed collar plates back along the cockpit sides as structural rails. Each rail ends at a separate raised, outboard back-weapon pivot. The arms swing underneath. Keep both hand weapons at v003 scale, both rear bells low beneath the rails and the hip jets clear. In a rear three-quarter drawing, raise one back weapon and keep the other stowed while both hands carry their weapons.

**Mechanical teeth.** Keep the short line of openings across the faceplate. Replace the ivory row below it with a partly covered ring of flat, blackened steel locking lugs on the neck bearing. Only the rubbed front edges catch light under the chin. As the head turns, the ends pass behind a fixed collar guard. At a glance those bright edges suggest clenched teeth; in close-up the square shoulders, gaps and circular track explain them.

**Red tissue through the frame.** Carry the upper arm’s oxblood fibers diagonally down the flanks, from the ribs toward the opposite hip, disappearing beneath the belly plate. Expose broader fans around the outer hips and thighs, then narrow cords behind the knees and at the heel. Keep steel around the forearms, shins, weapon pivots and exhausts. During a side boost the collar stays on aim as the hips shift under it. From behind, the red band above the catching hip tightens; the one across the other flank gathers into folds. On foot that shift alternates with each loaded step.

**References used.** The v003 sheet supplies the stamped mask, short face openings, split collar, marked upper arms, slotted fasteners and striated shoulder material. The owner’s marked portrait identifies the mouth, lettering and circular hardware that led to v003. The neck bearing, narrower hull and diagonal fibers are proposals for the next drawing. [Marked mask study, v003](assets/face-study/marked-mask-v003.png) · [Owner’s circled portrait](references/face-study/smooth-mask-owner-markup.png)

items.title: Recessed cockpit · Front and rear three-quarter, v002
items.alt: Front and rear views of a dark gray-green mech. Two angled chest plates frame a small pewter head. Burgundy shoulder fibers wrap the exposed arm bearings.
items.body:
Two angled hull plates flank the recessed pilot hatch. The side optic catches light behind the split collar, and burgundy fibers wrap the shoulder bearing beneath overlapping guards. The back view shows the attachment arms, the closed rear panel of the missile cassette and the paired booster bells. The legs and equipment still closely resemble Counterpart. The face reads chiefly through the narrow brow and the side optic; changes of relief across the mask are subtle at sheet size.

**Direct image inputs.** The [first sheet](assets/face-study/front-rear-v001.png) supplied the chassis and view layout. The smooth-mask crop informed the face relief, and the ribbed portrait informed the overlap of the shoulder guards and flexing tissue. Counterpart’s proportions entered through the first sheet. Generated with the built-in ImageGen tool. [Smooth-mask crop](references/pinterest/smooth-mask-788411478568823397.jpg) · [Ribbed shoulder portrait](references/pinterest/ribbed-chest-788411478568840783.jpg)

[Open full-resolution PNG](assets/face-study/front-rear-v002.png)
items.prompt:
Edit the two-view mech concept sheet in IMAGE 1. Keep both views of the SAME machine, same relative size and staging, materials, independent back pivots, low booster bells, outer hip nozzles, strong walking legs, and the four modular weapon positions. The machine is from the same foundry as an earlier frame but now needs ITS OWN hull tooling and facial identity. Rework the FRONT AND BACK consistently:

CHASSIS: replace the existing broad flat chest with TWO narrow fore-to-aft sponsons flanking a deep, recessed trapezoidal pilot pod. The new core has a shallow V of open space between the front ends of the two sponsons, with the pilot hatch deeper inside the V. The sponsons double as the foundation of the back weapon rails. Delete the conspicuous tow ring centered on the chest; replace it with a plain recessed service panel with two offset latches. On the knees use small, blunt rectangular graphite caps on steel hinges in both views. Remove both bright crescent knee guards and remove the yellow 17-like markings. Retain the useful industrial weight and family of joints but change the major plate shapes. Use restrained charcoal and oxidized gray-green on the new hull.

FACE: the second input is a close reference for VERY SHALLOW facial relief across worn metal. Draw the small pewter head a fraction more upright in its split collar. Give its crown a gently flattened brow that rolls through two shallow, asymmetrical changes of surface and tapers into a slightly off-center chinlike rim. Raking light makes it look very faintly like a face up close. It should feel machine-pressed, neither a human/sculpted face nor a featureless ball. Let the small amber sensor be a recessed glint visible through an actual notch in the near collar, not a conspicuous protruding eyeball. Size and placement of head within shoulders stay compact. Work with the form of the second image without copying its accessories or expression.

ARMS: image 3 is a close reference for how one rigid plate fits over a muscular joint. Give one shoulder a clear layered fan of burgundy bands winding around a large dark steel bearing beneath two sliding armor leaves. Keep the powerful clear grip on both vehicle-scale hand weapons. Show the machine's left hand pulse projector slightly lifted to load the shoulder, accelerator settled lower in its right. Traceable forearm/wrist/grip on both sides.

In rear view show the solid rear closures on the stowed right cassette, front cell doors face along the mech's gaze away from the viewer. Retain clearly mounted back weapons, right cassette lower and stowed and left twin-rail unit raised; keep their sides consistent across both views. Clean pale ground and calm shadows, no writing or annotations. Keep the large front view and small rear three-quarter full figure. One finished revised sheet.

items.title: First chassis study · Front and rear three-quarter, v001
items.alt: An industrial mech in front and rear views with a smooth metal head, red shoulder fibers, a chest shackle and pale crescent-marked knee guards.
items.body:
The collar and shoulder bearings read at a distance. The chest shackle, knee markings and rear cassette copied several identifiable features of Counterpart. The second sheet reworks those areas.

**Direct image inputs.** Counterpart’s foundry image supplied the fleet’s armor and limb proportions. The mask crop supplied a cue for facial relief and the ribbed portrait informed the shoulder joint. Generated with the built-in ImageGen tool. [Counterpart, foundry v001](assets/counterpart/foundry-v001.png) · [Smooth-mask crop](references/pinterest/smooth-mask-788411478568823397.jpg) · [Ribbed shoulder portrait](references/pinterest/ribbed-chest-788411478568840783.jpg)

[Open full-resolution PNG](assets/face-study/front-rear-v001.png)
items.prompt:
Derive a sibling chassis from the FIRST supplied image, the existing Counterpart game mech. Paint a two-view industrial design study, landscape format about 3:2. BOTH renderings depict the same newly reworked frame and same modular loadout. Retain the family character of the first image: serviceable dark folded armor, practical thickness, distinct weight-bearing hips and powerful flexible legs, broad feet, hefty wrist interfaces, weapon and thruster scale. Deliberately redesign its upper hull, head, collar and articulating arms. The cockpit now projects aft instead of a big forward slab. Preserve the unmistakable scale of a piloted armored vehicle. No replicated serials, knee dents or mirror-symmetry motif.

Take two tightly scoped cues from the other supplied pictures. SECOND (smooth gray mask): the eerie, ambiguous facial planes just under an uninterrupted surface. Interpret that quality in a small mildly asymmetric pewter sensor fairing, with almost effaced relief only visible in grazing light. Crown barely above shoulders. Its lower sides descend between a pair of short folded steel collar guards bolted to the front hull. Slight turn of the head reveals a recessed low amber optic THROUGH A VISIBLE NARROW GAP in the near guard. The edge of the fairing continues under this rim. The front still suggests a face with all lights off. No sculpted nose, eyebrows, eyelids, mouth, cheekbone openings, deep eye sockets, human skull or blank oversize hockey mask. Do not import the second image's spikes or alien silhouette. THIRD (ribbed portrait): translate the overlap between flexible tissue and hard shoulder surfaces into real mech articulation. A dark wine-colored fan of taut fibers winds around a steel bearing; fibers shorten across one edge as one arm rotates its emitter upward. Two separated outer guard plates slide past one another like pieces of an industrial housing, revealing a strip of muscle deep in the joint. Distinct upper arm, elbow, forearm, wrist, articulated hand. Keep fibers integrated and mostly protected. Do not copy the portrait's costume, ribs across the entire torso, exact anatomy or signature face. For overall style, favor first image heavily.

LEFT ~60% of sheet: large straight frontal study, head to upper thighs, showing both shoulders, both arms and hands. Bilateral weight and measured vehicle proportions. Readable small head without blowing its scale up: crop the shot, not the design. A massive square-section accelerator in anatomical RIGHT hand (front sheet image left); a shorter flared pulse emitter in anatomical LEFT (front image right) with elbow rising slightly higher. Each is gripped beneath its housing and clears the torso. On high separate back mounts a squat missile cassette on anatomical RIGHT and a folded twin-rail weapon on anatomical LEFT. Avoid covering the shoulder joint with a carried gun.

RIGHT ~40%: smaller full-body REAR three-quarter view looking obliquely at the back of the same machine, head turned slightly, both broad split feet down. Clear daylight between attachment point of each back weapon and the arm below. Trace one rigid chassis rail from rear corner of the cockpit up to a thick exposed circular hinge, then short swing arm and weapon. Show the left folding twin-rail launcher raised at this pivot and the right compact cassette stowed close. With this camera rearward, keep side assignments correct. Show paired main booster bells slung below the rear core, and a separate short flush lateral jet at the outer hip. Back of waist is not all occupied by guns. Graphite-sleeved thighs carry the cockpit in a slight walking crouch, feet under hips. Distinct front and rear views, hands in both views each grip the same two different guns as labeled above.

Boutique game art-department design plate, crafted realism, deliberate grouping of details against large calm metal planes; grime concentrated at edges and sliders, restrained fleet color petrol-black and gunmetal with pewter fairing. Neutral pale warm-gray studio ground, soft contact shadow only, no hangar or horizon. Raking soft light reads the surface planes in the mask, enough fill to read dark mechanical bearings. Uncluttered margin between the views. No added labels, text, graphics, arrows, occult emblems or third figure.

items.title: Head and collar
items.body: A softly convex, dull pewter cover protects the sensor carriage. Two shallow changes of plane suggest a pair of eyes in grazing light. The working optic sits low at the side, where it can see through the gap between the two collar guards as the head turns. The guards bolt to the core and carry the same kind of folded edges and accessible fasteners as the shoulder housings. Give the head its own outline in that gap, legible from the front and from the flank.

items.title: Shoulders, arms and load
items.body:
Keep the compact cockpit deep from front to back. Set the head low enough that the crown sits just above the upper shoulder line. Behind it, two steel rails rise from the cockpit’s rear corners. Each rail ends at an exposed circular pivot, with a short swing arm carrying a back weapon. Leave a visible gap between each weapon pivot and the rotating arm joint below. A rear three-quarter view should let the eye trace each weapon all the way to the hull.

A fan of dark contractile fibers wraps the shoulder bearing. As one hand rolls its heavy emitter up to aim, those fibers bunch and the overlapping shoulder guard slides a little over them. The bearing, guard and upper arm form one working joint. Give the other hand a long, square-section accelerator. With both grippers lowered the wrists reach roughly to the tops of the thighs. A compact cassette and a folding rail unit sit on the high rear pivots.

items.title: Silhouette and movement
items.body: Bring back the weight through the hips and upper legs. Bowed thighs and broad heel blocks carry the core in short deliberate steps. Twin booster bells tuck under the rear weapon rails and a smaller side jet sits in each outer hip. Through a lateral boost the hips shift under a level collar while the gun arms hold their aim. The leading foot catches the weight as the jet cuts.

items.title: First visual study
items.body:
Compare the frame with Counterpart for the apparent thickness of the plates, the scale of the mount pivots, and how much weight the legs seem to carry. For direct image input, use Counterpart’s foundry view for those fleet details, the smooth-mask crop for shallow facial relief, and the ribbed portrait for the meeting of hard and flexible surfaces at the shoulder. Keep the full-body portrait available for a head-scale check.

Show the head, chest and both arms from the front, with a smaller full-body rear three-quarter view of the same frame. Stow one back weapon and raise the other. From that angle the eye should be able to follow the raised weapon down its pivot to the cockpit frame and still pick out the low rear booster. The machine should work in both views before adding its rite.

items.title: References used
items.body:
Counterpart’s foundry view is the proposed fleet reference for armor thickness, visible weapon pivots and load-bearing leg proportions. [Counterpart, foundry v001](assets/counterpart/foundry-v001.png)

The smooth-mask crop informs the subtlety of the relief across the face. The split collar and the optic visible through its gap belong to this frame. [Smooth mask](references/pinterest/smooth-mask-788411478568823397.jpg) · [Original pin](https://www.pinterest.com/pin/788411478568823397/)

The ribbed portrait shows how a hard outer arm plate can sit against tissue that moves under load. [Ribbed portrait](references/pinterest/ribbed-chest-788411478568840783.jpg) · [Original pin](https://www.pinterest.com/pin/788411478568840783/)

The full-body view is a secondary check on head scale. Sitter’s first lift was reviewed for the proportion and mounting issues the owner identified. [Full-body view](references/pinterest/smooth-mask-full-body-788411478568840781.jpg) · [Original pin](https://www.pinterest.com/pin/788411478568840781/) · [Sitter’s first lift](assets/sitter/first-lift-v001.png)
